title: Nvidia investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek for AI chip partnership

questions.question: Will NVIDIA complete its announced $3.5 billion investment in MediaTek through convertible bonds by January 31, 2027?
questions.why_it_matters: A completed $3.5 billion investment would be a material deployment of NVIDIA capital and deepen its strategic relationship with MediaTek. The partnership could also help embed NVIDIA’s interconnect technology in custom-chip data-center designs and extend its reach into consumer and automotive computing.
questions.why_not_already_covered: The existing questions cover other NVIDIA investments and commitments, including investments in Lancium, NAVER, and SB Energy, but none asks whether NVIDIA completes this MediaTek investment. Its completion is a distinct transaction outcome; the article reports an announcement, not that the investment has been completed.
questions.how_and_when_to_check: Check by January 31, 2027, an analyst check date at NVIDIA’s FY2027 year-end; the article states no completion date. Review announcements and filings from NVIDIA and MediaTek for confirmation that the convertible-bond investment closed, including its amount and terms.

evidence.quote: Nvidia announced on Monday that it is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek through convertible bonds, deepening a partnership with the Taiwanese chipmaker that spans AI data center infrastructure, consumer PCs, and automotive platforms.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article reports the announced investment amount and instrument, as well as the partnership’s breadth. It establishes the transaction to track but does not say it has closed.
evidence.original_speaker: The article’s opening report; no individual speaker is named.

evidence.quote: As part of the expanded agreement, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia's NVLink Fusion platform, which is designed to help hyperscalers, cloud providers, and AI model developers build custom accelerator chips that connect into Nvidia's rack-scale data center systems, the companies said.
evidence.what_it_shows: The companies’ stated agreement includes MediaTek’s adoption of NVLink Fusion, connecting the investment to NVIDIA’s strategic effort to position its interconnect in custom-accelerator systems.
evidence.original_speaker: NVIDIA and MediaTek, as reported by the article.

evidence.quote: The deal also extends their existing collaboration on Nvidia RTX Spark and DGX Spark chips for consumer and enterprise PCs, as well as AI-powered automotive platforms built around MediaTek's Dimensity Auto line.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article says the deal extends collaboration across PC and automotive platforms, indicating strategic reach beyond data centers.
evidence.original_speaker: The article’s report; no individual speaker is named.

evidence.quote: "AI is transforming every computing platform — from the world's largest AI factories to the PC and the car," Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement. "Together, we're building platforms that bring NVIDIA accelerated computing to new markets and give customers the freedom to create differentiated AI systems at enormous scale."
evidence.what_it_shows: Huang presents the partnership as a way to extend NVIDIA accelerated computing into additional markets. This is strategic rationale, not confirmation of investment completion.
evidence.original_speaker: Jensen Huang, NVIDIA founder and CEO.

evidence.quote: MediaTek vice chairman and CEO Rick Tsai said in a statement that Nvidia's investment "strengthens a collaboration that spans cloud AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive in the era of physical AI."
evidence.what_it_shows: MediaTek’s CEO characterizes the investment as strengthening collaboration across cloud, local-computing, and automotive markets; the statement does not confirm the investment has closed.
evidence.original_speaker: Rick Tsai, MediaTek vice chairman and CEO.

evidence.quote: Nvidia sees the deal as a way to anchor its interconnect technology and hardware architecture within AI data center build-outs at a moment when many of its biggest customers are pursuing their own custom silicon, according to Bloomberg . MediaTek is competing with Broadcom and Marvell Technology for business helping data center operators design custom silicon.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bloomberg’s account describes the deal’s strategic purpose: securing a role for NVIDIA’s interconnect and architecture as customers pursue custom silicon. MediaTek’s competition for custom-chip design business provides context for the partnership’s potential competitive significance.
evidence.original_speaker: Bloomberg, as attributed by the article; the characterization of NVIDIA’s strategic purpose is not quoted directly from the company.

evidence.quote: The NVLink Fusion platform gives customers a foundation for building custom accelerator chips — combining NVLink connectivity, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, and rack-scale integration — so they can focus engineering resources on differentiated compute rather than surrounding infrastructure, the companies said.
evidence.what_it_shows: The companies describe the platform capabilities that underpin the claimed strategic value of MediaTek adopting NVLink Fusion.
evidence.original_speaker: NVIDIA and MediaTek, as reported by the article.

evidence.quote: Nvidia has been investing in companies across the AI supply chain , including power infrastructure developer Lancium and chip designer Marvell Technology.
evidence.what_it_shows: The article places the MediaTek investment within NVIDIA’s broader pattern of investing across the AI supply chain; it does not establish completion of this particular investment.
evidence.original_speaker: The article’s report; no individual speaker is named.

evidence.quote: The deal echoes terms Nvidia recently secured with Amazon, which signed on to incorporate 2 million Nvidia components into its infrastructure and agreed to run Nvidia's connection technology in tandem with chips it develops internally, according to Bloomberg.
evidence.what_it_shows: Bloomberg’s comparison offers context for NVIDIA’s approach to working with customers that develop their own chips, but it does not provide confirmation or a closing timetable for the MediaTek investment.
evidence.original_speaker: Bloomberg, as attributed by the article.

evidence.quote: MediaTek had previously partnered with Alphabet's Google and collaborated with Nvidia on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip that powers the DGX Spark developer computer, the companies said.
evidence.what_it_shows: The companies’ account indicates prior MediaTek experience with Google and an existing NVIDIA collaboration, providing context for the expanded relationship but not confirmation of the investment’s completion.
evidence.original_speaker: NVIDIA and MediaTek, as reported by the article.

article:
Nvidia announced on Monday that it is investing $3.5 billion in MediaTek through convertible bonds, deepening a partnership with the Taiwanese chipmaker that spans AI data center infrastructure, consumer PCs, and automotive platforms.
As part of the expanded agreement, MediaTek will adopt Nvidia's NVLink Fusion platform, which is designed to help hyperscalers, cloud providers, and AI model developers build custom accelerator chips that connect into Nvidia's rack-scale data center systems, the companies said. The deal also extends their existing collaboration on Nvidia RTX Spark and DGX Spark chips for consumer and enterprise PCs, as well as AI-powered automotive platforms built around MediaTek's Dimensity Auto line.
"AI is transforming every computing platform — from the world's largest AI factories to the PC and the car," Nvidia founder and CEO Jensen Huang said in a statement. "Together, we're building platforms that bring NVIDIA accelerated computing to new markets and give customers the freedom to create differentiated AI systems at enormous scale."
MediaTek vice chairman and CEO Rick Tsai said in a statement that Nvidia's investment "strengthens a collaboration that spans cloud AI infrastructure, local AI computing and automotive in the era of physical AI."
Nvidia sees the deal as a way to anchor its interconnect technology and hardware architecture within AI data center build-outs at a moment when many of its biggest customers are pursuing their own custom silicon, according to Bloomberg . MediaTek is competing with Broadcom and Marvell Technology for business helping data center operators design custom silicon.
The NVLink Fusion platform gives customers a foundation for building custom accelerator chips — combining NVLink connectivity, high-bandwidth memory, advanced packaging, and rack-scale integration — so they can focus engineering resources on differentiated compute rather than surrounding infrastructure, the companies said.
Nvidia has been investing in companies across the AI supply chain , including power infrastructure developer Lancium and chip designer Marvell Technology. The deal echoes terms Nvidia recently secured with Amazon, which signed on to incorporate 2 million Nvidia components into its infrastructure and agreed to run Nvidia's connection technology in tandem with chips it develops internally, according to Bloomberg.
MediaTek had previously partnered with Alphabet's Google and collaborated with Nvidia on the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip that powers the DGX Spark developer computer, the companies said.
